# AI-Generated Images and Human-Drawn Art

This graph compares the image counts reported by the two datasets. It does
**not** measure how much art was created overall: TWIGMA counts AI-generated
images shared on Twitter from January 2021 to March 2023, while AI-ArtBench is
a curated benchmark with human-drawn and AI-generated images.

## Dataset image counts

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

image_counts <- tibble::tibble(
  image_type = c("AI-generated Twitter images",
                 "AI-generated images",
                 "Human-drawn images"),
  count = c(800000, 120000, 60000)
)

ggplot(image_counts, aes(x = reorder(image_type, count), y = count,
                         fill = image_type)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = \(x) format(x, big.mark = ",",
                                          scientific = FALSE)) +
  labs(
    title = "Image counts reported by the two datasets",
    subtitle = "Dataset sample sizes—not total art creation",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of images",
    caption = paste(
      "TWIGMA reports about 800,000 AI-generated images posted on Twitter.",
      "AI-ArtBench reports 120,000 AI-generated and 60,000 human-drawn images.",
      "The sources have different collection methods and time coverage."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Sources: [TWIGMA on Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/11374087) and
[AI-ArtBench on Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/ravidussilva/real-ai-art).
